What

What Tree Removal Actually Involves

Tree removal isn't just felling and walking away. Here's what a proper Roubic removal looks like from start to finish.

Tree removal is the complete elimination of a standing, leaning, or partially-failed tree — including felling or top-down dismantling of the crown, sectional lowering of the trunk to protect adjacent targets, stump grinding (or full-excavation stump removal where re-planting is planned), and full haul-off of debris. When the job is finished, the site should be a level grade with no standing wood, no debris piles, and no stump tripping hazards.

Step 1

Assess

Crown condition, lean, root plate, adjacent targets

Step 2

Fell / Lower

Ground felling or top-down sectional rigging

Step 3

Chip

Full debris haul via owned Bandit chipper

Step 4

Grind

Stump ground to 6–12" below grade (optional)

Step 5

Grade

Site cleanup + final walk-through with client

Why

Why NE Ohio Homeowners Need Removal

The most common removal drivers we see across Cuyahoga and Geauga counties — none of them are theoretical. Every one of these appears on 30–40% of the estimates Aaron walks each month.

  • EAB-killed ash treesEmerald ash borer wiped out most of NE Ohio's ash canopy 2008–2012. Standing dead ash goes structurally unsafe in one growing season.
  • Trees leaning toward structuresRoot plates saturate, wind loads shift — leaning trees fail in the storms we get every March through May.
  • Storm-damaged treesSplit crowns and lightning-struck trunks that survived one storm rarely survive the next.
  • Trees near utilitiesContact with power lines is a coordination job — Roubic clears with the utility company, not around them.

How

How Roubic Approaches Every Removal

Same 8-step process on a $400 small removal or a $5,000 crane job. It's the reason our clients call the same Roubic number for two generations.

8

What If You Wait

The Cost of Deferring a Hazard Tree

Every one of these is quantified from actual insurance-claim data + village fine records in Cuyahoga and Geauga counties.

Insurance Deductible on Limb-Fall

When a limb falls in a storm, your policy typically covers post-fall damage but you're on the hook for the $1,000–$2,500 deductible — often more than proactive removal.

Post-Fall Premium Hikes

Homeowner's insurance premiums frequently rise 10–20% after any claim — including tree-fall claims — for 3–5 years.

Foundation + Driveway Damage

Root uplift from a leaning tree can damage foundations, septic lines, and driveways. Repairs typically start at $5,000+ — well past what a removal costs.

Municipal Fines

Pepper Pike, Moreland Hills, Gates Mills — canopy threatening right-of-way generates village citations if left unremediated after notice.

EAB Stability Degradation

An EAB-killed ash goes from "standing but dead" to "structurally compromised" in one growing season. What removes for $700 this fall removes for $2,000 next fall as a hazard job.

Liability Exposure

If a known hazard tree falls on a neighbor's property or a passer-by, courts have found homeowners negligent for not addressing documented risks.

Common Removal Questions

Tree Removal FAQ

Seven answers before you book. Every one from Aaron's actual 2026 estimate conversations.

Do I need a permit to remove a tree on my property?
Depends on the village. Pepper Pike requires a permit for any tree 24" DBH or larger. Gates Mills 18". Moreland Hills has separate rules. Roubic handles permit filing in-house — it's included in your estimate for permit-required villages. Auburn Township, Solon, Chagrin Falls (residential), Beachwood, Orange, Bainbridge Township, Shaker Heights, Chesterland, Mayfield, South Russell — no residential permit needed for private-property removals.
How fast can Roubic respond to an emergency tree removal?
Our 24/7 emergency line is answered directly. Tier 1 cities (Auburn Township, Pepper Pike, Chagrin Falls, Moreland Hills, Solon) — typically 1–2 hour after-hours response. Business-hours response across the full 40-mile radius averages 2–4 hours.
Does homeowner's insurance cover tree removal?
Generally no for proactive removals — that's your out-of-pocket cost. Yes for post-fall damage cleanup after a storm event. Yes for tree-on-structure situations. Roubic delivers a full insurance-documentation packet (photos, written scope, signed estimate) on every storm / structure-impact job for direct submission to your carrier.
How much does it cost to remove a large tree in NE Ohio?
Aaron's 2026 confirmed pricing: small tree under 30 ft $400–$800; medium 30–60 ft $650–$950; large 60–80 ft $850–$2,000; very-large or crane-required $2,000–$5,000+. Every estimate is free with in-person property walk. Full breakdown in the pricing table above.
What happens to the wood after removal — do you haul it away?
Standard is full haul-off via our Bandit chipper — nothing left in your driveway. If you want the wood (for firewood or a specific project), we cut to your specified lengths and stack. Just tell us during the estimate. No price difference either way.
Do you handle stump grinding as part of the removal?
Optional add-on. Stump grinding is $275 minimum plus $8 per inch of stump diameter, ground to 6–12" below grade. Full-excavation stump removal (for re-planting or hardscape) priced separately. Roubic can also leave the stump if that's what you want.
Can you remove a tree touching a power line?
Yes — but we coordinate with the utility company first. Trees touching or leaning into primary lines require the utility to de-energize or use their line-clearance crew for the wire clearance portion. Roubic handles the removal after clearance. Never a good DIY.
